From: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
To: rachel.kim@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 7 Oct 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Redwood MSA + Order Form redlines (output & training questions)

Thanks Rachel — quick thoughts below. Inline follow-ups at bottom.

Short answer: we should not assign title to Customer Output. We can offer a limited, non-exclusive, worldwide license to use Customer Output for the narrowly defined productization purposes Novatek requests, with strict attribution/usage limits, and explicit exclusions for third-party resale. Assignment opens IP governance and downstream risk we cannot accept.

Training/Feedback license: we can support an opt-in, time-boxed feedback/training license under these constraints:
- Opt-in must be a separately signed box on the Order Form (no implicit opt-in).
- Scope limited to improvements to a named model family, not for generalized model releases.
- Redactions/sanitization obligations on customer side for PII/high-risk data (we'll include example checklist).
- Customer can revoke opt-in with 90 days' notice; any in-flight retraining may be excluded from revocation if already committed (clarify in order form).

Evidence for pre-contract training: we can provide the following artifacts without exposing internal pipelines:
- A signed attestation that data from public customers was not included in model updates dated before effective date (high level).
- Token-level aggregate telemetry around training corpora provenance (e.g., percentage from public web vs licensed corpora) but only as percentages to avoid revealing models or datasets.
- SOC 2 Type II report excerpt (they provided SOC2 excerpt; we can reciprocate our last audited period) — redact internal details.

Risks & negotiation posture:
- If they persist on assignment, escalate to VP Legal / Sales Leadership; consider commercial offset (price uplift, escrow).
- For opt-in training, require clear revocation mechanics and audit rights limited to compliance review (not full access to training corpora).

Action items:
- Ben: propose commercial compromise (license + training opt-in fee or rate uplift) by Friday EOD.
- Aditya: draft a one-page evidence summary and an example attestation we can share by Monday.
- Rachel/Laura: propose precise clause text for Order Form and MSA redlines (we'll avoid assignment language) by Monday.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: rachel.kim@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 7 Oct 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Redwood MSA + Order Form redlines (output & training questions)

All — thanks Laura, that stance works for GTM. Quick commercial sketch for Novatek:

1) Output: non-exclusive worldwide license for Customer Output for productization, with prohibition on sublicensing/transfer and attribution clause.
2) Training opt-in: one-time enrollment fee + per-token training uplift for any production retraining that includes their data (will propose numbers offline).
3) Evidence: offer SOC2 excerpt + signed attestation + high-level provenance percentages (Aditya to confirm this is feasible).
4) If Novatek insists on assignment, offer a limited assignment for narrow outputs tied to a single product line for a short term + higher fee + escrow of derivative model weights — otherwise decline.

I'll draft the commercial response and a revised Order Form section and share tomorrow morning. If Laura is comfortable with the clause we propose, I'll send to Mia with an inline explanation and the proposed procurement timeline (Novatek procurement cut-off: next Thursday).

Ben Carter
Principal Sales Lead
Redwood Inference
